pictures.scene: Hendrick ter Brugghen, King David Playing the Harp — the old king in a spiked gold crown and a great red and gold brocade mantle over white, his white beard on his chest and his eyes lifted, one lined hand reaching in among the strings of the tall harp, the singers crowding in close behind him over their music, a Shiggaion of David which he sang to the LORD concerning the words of Cush a Benjamite
pictures.name: pd_brugghen_king_david

pictures.scene: Willem de Poorter, Saul and David in the Cave — the king standing in the mouth of the cave in a dark red velvet mantle and a gold-crowned white turban, his hand put out toward the young man who has gone down on one knee in front of him in armor and a rose cloak with his cap in his hand, a soldier watching from the dark at the back, O LORD my God I take refuge in You, save me and deliver me from all my pursuers
pictures.name: pd_de_poorter_saul_and_david_in_the_cave

pictures.scene: George Stubbs, A Lion Attacking a Horse — the white horse down on the rock with its head thrown round and its mouth open screaming, the tawny lion up on its back with its claws set in the shoulder and its teeth in the mane, the black crags and the storm shutting the whole place in behind them, or they will shred my soul like a lion and tear me to pieces with no one to rescue me
pictures.name: pd_stubbs_a_lion_attacking_a_horse

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Elderly Man in Prayer — the old man in a plain grey-brown robe with his eyes closed and his white beard spread down his chest, his two worn hands pressed palm to palm in the one patch of light, an open book lying out on the table under them, O LORD my God if I have done this, if injustice is on my hands
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_elderly_man_in_prayer

pictures.scene: Giotto, The Kiss of Judas — the betrayer wrapping Christ round in his wide yellow cloak and putting his face up to His, the two of them looking straight into each other, the gold halo behind Christ and the whole crowd pressed in around them with clubs and torches and spears standing up into the blue sky, if I have rewarded my ally with evil, if I have plundered my foe without cause
pictures.name: pd_giotto_the_kiss_of_judas

pictures.scene: Jan van Huchtenburg, Cavalry Battle — the horseman in a plumed hat driving his black horse clean over the fallen with his sword run out at full stretch, a red standard flying back off his shoulder, a white horse going down on its knees beyond him and the trampled ground in front filled with men and a dead horse lying together, then may my enemy pursue me and overtake me, may he trample me to the ground
pictures.name: pd_van_huchtenburgh_cavalry_battle

pictures.scene: Martin Johnson Heade, Approaching Thunderstorm — the whole sky gone black over the bay with one thin fork of lightning dropping out of the cloud, the water lying flat and dark as slate under it, one man alone in a little rowing boat out in the middle of it, and a white sail folded over a rock on the sand in front, and leave my honor in the dust, arise O LORD in Your anger
pictures.name: pd_heade_approaching_thunderstorm

pictures.scene: Bartolome Bermejo, Saint Michael Triumphant over the Devil — the archangel in gilded plate armor and a flying crimson mantle standing with both feet on the scaled dragon, his sword swung up over his head and a crystal shield held down in his other hand, his wings burning orange and red against the gold, the kneeling donor at his side with an open book, rise up against the fury of my enemies, awake my God and ordain judgment
pictures.name: pd_bermejo_saint_michael_triumphant_over_the_devil

pictures.scene: Jan Brueghel the Elder, The Sermon on the Mount — the whole hillside packed with people in every kind of dress, hats and white caps and ruffs crowding away in rows, and up on the rise among them the one small figure in pale robes with a faint halo and His hands out, speaking, the great green trees standing over the whole gathering, let the assembled peoples gather around You, take Your seat over them on high
pictures.name: pd_brueghel_bergrede

pictures.scene: Christ in Majesty, Sant Climent de Taull — the great Romanesque fresco figure seated inside the painted oval, His cross-marked halo filling the top of the arch, one hand raised in blessing and the other holding the open book that says I am the light of the world, His robes laid out in bands of blue and grey and red, the LORD judges the peoples, vindicate me O LORD
pictures.name: pd_taull_pantocrator

pictures.scene: Georges de La Tour, The Cheat with the Ace of Diamonds — the cheat sitting with his back to us in a pale yellow coat and a black sash, his face turned away in profile and his eyes slid sideways at the others, his hand down behind his back drawing the hidden card out of his belt where no one at the table can see it, according to my righteousness and integrity, put an end to the evil of the wicked
pictures.name: pd_de_la_tour_the_cheat_with_the_ace_of_diamonds

pictures.scene: Johannes Vermeer, Woman Holding a Balance — the woman in a white linen hood and a blue fur-trimmed jacket standing quiet at the table with her eyes down, the little empty scales held level between her fingers and the pearls and gold lying out of the opened box beside her, the dark Last Judgment hanging on the wall at her shoulder, but establish the righteous, O righteous God who searches hearts and minds
pictures.name: pd_vermeer_balance

pictures.scene: Jan van Eyck, The Knights of Christ — the riders coming on in burnished plate armor with their lances held upright and the red-crossed banners and a white shield with the cross of Saint George carried up among them, the leading knight on a pale horse in jewelled harness, the crowned and turbaned heads of the company pressed in behind under the rocks, my shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart
pictures.name: pd_van_eyck_the_knights_of_christ

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Belshazzar's Feast — the king wheeling round at the table in a gold brocade robe and a crowned white turban, his mouth open and his eyes starting as he stares up at what has appeared on the wall, one arm flung out and the other knocking a gold dish over among the fruit and the spilled wine, God is a righteous judge and a God who feels indignation each day
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_belshazzars_feast

pictures.scene: Joseph Wright of Derby, The Blacksmith's Shop — the white-hot bar lying on the anvil throwing its light up into every face, two smiths in open shirts bent over it with their hammers raised and coming down, the sparks flying out across the dark forge, a boy shielding his eyes from the glare and the moon standing in the broken wall behind, if one does not repent God will sharpen His sword, He has bent and strung His bow
pictures.name: pd_wright_de_smidse

pictures.scene: Johan Christian Dahl, Eruption of Vesuvius — the crater burst wide open along the whole ridge, the lava running out red and gold under a tower of smoke that fills the sky, little sparks of fire thrown up into the cloud, and one tiny figure in a tall hat standing out on the cinders watching it, He has prepared His deadly weapons, He ordains His arrows with fire
pictures.name: pd_dahl_eruption_of_vesuvius

pictures.scene: Georges de La Tour, The Fortune Teller — the young man in a buff coat and a red sash standing with his eyes slid sideways and his mind on the telling, while the women pressed close around him work their hands quietly at his belt, one lifting a coin away and another unhooking the gold medal on its chain, behold the wicked man travails with evil, he conceives trouble and births falsehood
pictures.name: pd_la_tour_the_fortune_teller

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Bird Trap — the frozen village under snow with the bare trees standing up through it, the skaters out on the ice behind, and down in the front corner the heavy door propped up on a stick over the bare ground with the string run off to the window and the birds hopping in under it, he has dug a hole and hollowed it out, he has fallen into a pit of his own making
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_strik

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Haman Recognizes His Fate — the man who built the gallows standing in a heavy red robe and a gold-banded turban with his eyes dropped and his face gone slack, one hand laid flat on his breast over the gold chain and the other hanging open at his side, the old bearded king watching him out of the dark at his shoulder, his trouble recoils on himself, and his violence falls on his own head
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_haman_recognizes_his_fate

pictures.scene: Jan van Eyck, The Singing Angels — the eight angels crowded shoulder to shoulder around the carved wooden lectern in heavy red and gold brocade copes clasped with jewels, their hair falling in curls under jewelled bands and little gold crosses, every mouth open on a different note and their eyes on the open book, I will thank the LORD for His righteousness and sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High
pictures.name: pd_van_eyck_the_singing_angels

lines.text: A Shiggaion of David,
which he sang to the LORD concerning the words of Cush, a Benjamite.
O LORD my God, I take refuge in You;
save me and deliver me from all my pursuers,
or they will shred my soul like a lion
and tear me to pieces with no one to rescue me.
O LORD my God, if I have done this,
if injustice is on my hands,
if I have rewarded my ally with evil,
if I have plundered my foe without cause,
then may my enemy pursue me and overtake me;
may he trample me to the ground
and leave my honor in the dust. Selah
Arise, O LORD, in Your anger;
rise up against the fury of my enemies.
Awake, my God, and ordain judgment.
Let the assembled peoples gather around You;
take Your seat over them on high.
The LORD judges the peoples;
vindicate me, O LORD,
according to my righteousness and integrity.
Put an end to the evil of the wicked,
but establish the righteous,
O righteous God who searches hearts and minds.
My shield is with God,
who saves the upright in heart.
God is a righteous judge
and a God who feels indignation each day.
If one does not repent, God will sharpen His sword;
He has bent and strung His bow.
He has prepared His deadly weapons;
He ordains His arrows with fire.
Behold, the wicked man travails with evil;
he conceives trouble and births falsehood.
He has dug a hole and hollowed it out;
he has fallen into a pit of his own making.
His trouble recoils on himself,
and his violence falls on his own head.
I will thank the LORD for His righteousness
and sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High.
